question: How fast do habits break?
title: Can agents break the habit?
headline: Can agents break the habit?

parts.headline: Habit Was the Moat. Agents Are Draining It.
parts.question: How fast do habits break?

call.line: Agents will drain weak consumer habits first. Back the rails (trust, records, distribution, compute), not the forgotten subscription.
actions: Flag businesses that live on inertia: forgotten subscriptions, commodity brands, ad-funded marketplaces.
Favor owners of trust, regulation, systems of record, distribution and compute.
Judge agent launches on retained users, transactions and fees, never on downloads.
flips: Meta reports agent downloads without retained users, transaction volume or fees.
The first tax season with agents shows households still paying Intuit for certainty.

against.name: Le Shrub
against.claim: Le Shrub questions whether Meta's Muse AI agent becoming popular so quickly is a big negative for OpenAI and Anthropic.

voices.name: Andrew Walker
voices.claim: Faced with two extreme camps on consumer AI agents (that they are massively overhyped versus that every consumer-facing company is a short because agents will eat their margins), Andrew Walker says both are too extreme but if forced to pick, they…

voices.name: Andrew Walker
voices.claim: AI agents make price-shopping and replacing skilled workers (e.g., using AI to edit a podcast instead of a consultant) easy, and if saving money is the core consumer use case for AI, this could have a deflationary impact on the consumer economy at…

voices.name: Tae Kim
voices.claim: As computer tool use rises, AI compute demand will explode just as it did when agentic coding took off, when reasoning models ramped, and when AI chatbots were first released.

voices.name: Tae Kim
voices.claim: Having used Muse over the past week, Tae Kim found problems in the quality and accuracy of its responses and found it hard to choose it over ChatGPT, and suspects others will feel the same way.

voices.name: Ren
voices.claim: Once an AI moves from surfacing a link to researching, deciding, executing and paying, it inserts itself between the customer and the business, potentially capturing an unusually valuable piece of the internet's discovery and transaction funnel.

voices.name: Ren
voices.claim: The unit of interaction is shifting from the prompt to the objective: instead of a chatbot loop of question-and-answer, Muse takes a goal, plans, executes, and only interrupts the user at decisions it isn't allowed to make alone.

against.name: Le Shrub
against.claim: Le Shrub questions whether Meta's Muse AI agent becoming popular so quickly is a big negative for OpenAI and Anthropic.

voices.name: Moses Sternstein
voices.claim: The data suggests that, for now, the story is 'App-Slop': AI has produced many more apps, but they are not successful apps in any meaningful sense.

voices.name: Moses Sternstein
voices.claim: Paid consumer AI adoption remains quite low even though it is growing, per Consumer Edge data showing roughly 3% adoption as of Q1, with younger people adopting at about 4x the rate of older people.

voices.name: David George
voices.claim: The creators argue OpenAI will prevail not because of best models, chips, cost-performance curve or even best product — though they think OpenAI has those — but because it is so good at creating new kinds of customers and has the most durable…

voices.name: David George
voices.claim: As of September 2026, the creators say intelligence-as-a-service product rankings are no longer the most important question; intelligence is everywhere and nearly anyone can do nearly anything, yet most people aren't yet, so awakening new behavior…

voices.name: Michael Spencer
voices.claim: Michael Spencer is not confident about Muse's odds of success, citing that only Anthropic has shown how to scale ARR so far in this Generative AI cycle, that the ratio of app downloads to actual users seems fairly low and suspicious, and that Meta…

voices.name: Michael Spencer
voices.claim: Generative AI's impact on the macro economy and labor market is a serious concern: higher inflation, less hiring, more anxiety, and a lack of ROI compared to the debt, capex and resulting AI bubble, with higher earnings masking dangerous…

against.name: Le Shrub
against.claim: Le Shrub says that, like an everyday 'normie', they want something simple and non-geeky for daily tasks rather than a highly advanced model that solves difficult math problems, implying simpler consumer AI tools like Muse may win out over more…

voices.name: Andrew Walker
voices.claim: Andrew Walker says they cannot watch how easy Muse is to use and how fast its downloads have taken off and conclude it won't have a big impact on the consumer economy.

voices.name: Andrew Walker
voices.claim: Andrew Walker suggests that Muse acting as a layer that decides where consumer spend goes is a massive threat and opportunity for retailers, noting as evidence that Amazon banned Muse.

voices.name: Tae Kim
voices.claim: On the owner of the agent and on the rails beneath it.

tests.event: Booking reports room nights and direct mix; the result tests whether the agent or the incumbent owns the booking.

source.ref: Company earnings calendar, date via Financial Modeling Prep

resolver.rule: Read room nights and the direct mix from the release and the call; room nights above the year-earlier quarter and a direct share at or above the year-earlier share resolves confirmed, a decline in either resolves refuted.
resolver.question: Did Booking Holdings report September-quarter room nights above the September quarter of 2025, with a direct-channel share of bookings no lower than the share it reported a year earlier?

source.label: Booking Holdings investor relations, third-quarter 2026 results

resolver.ambiguity: If Booking gives no direct-mix figure for the quarter, or reports after November 30, 2026, the test is inconclusive, reviewed by the owner.

tests.event: Nike holds its investor day; margin targets and demand plans show how much selling still assumes human choice.

resolver.rule: Yes if the presentation, press release or webcast transcript on Nike's investor-relations site states a margin target with a number and a fiscal year beyond 2027; the test resolves confirmed on yes and refuted on no. How much of the demand plan still assumes a person choosing (stores, app, wholesale, marketing) is the owner's reading from the same materials and goes in the Result, not in the verdict.
resolver.question: Did Nike, in the materials published for its investor day of November 16 and 17, 2026, state a numerical operating-margin or gross-margin target for a fiscal year beyond fiscal 2027?

source.label: Nike investor relations, investor day presentation and press release

resolver.ambiguity: If the investor day is postponed past November 30, 2026, or the materials are not public, the test is inconclusive, reviewed by the owner.
